newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Police beef up security on eve of Lisbon summit.
newsitem.headline: Police beef up security on eve of Lisbon summit.

text.p: Police blocked entrances to Lisbon's luxury hotels on Sunday and strengthened patrols on the streets and at the airport on the eve of a pan-European security summit in the Portuguese capital.

"Rapid intervention" police armed with sub-machine guns guarded a conference centre where leaders from the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) were to meet on Monday and Tuesday.

Traffic was light in downtown Lisbon as many residents took advantage of the summit to spend a long weekend away from the capital. A public holiday has been declared for Monday to coincide with the event.
Cars trickled across the April 25 bridge over the River Tagus, a major link to the capital, which is normally congested on Sunday.

The flags of member nations fluttered in welcome along Liberty Avenue, Lisbon's main boulevard, which was being patrolled by small groups of Public Security Police (PSP) wearing red arm-bands. Normally the police presence in Lisbon is light.
Police cordoned off entrances to the big hotels around Liberty Avenue where many heads of state were to stay.
"I've never seen this many police in the streets of Lisbon before. Portugal is such a peaceful country," said a taxi driver.
